unmapped_findings: The solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels of all three Al contents (15Al, 17Al, 19Al) are single-phase α (BCC) with no resolvable γ (FCC); the α grain structure is markedly refined as Al increases from 15 to 19 at.% (figure_003, b0040).

The hardness of the solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content (15Al = 253.4 HV, 17Al = 259.8 HV, 19Al = 263.8 HV), attributed to the solid-solution strengthening effect (b0036, Tables 2-4).

The 15Al solution-treated solid-solution state is explicitly identified as the soft parent state of all subsequent aging treatments; its aliases include 'soft state' and 'ST' (b0017, process definition).

The elastic modulus of 164 GPa for the 15Al alloy (measured through compressive stress-strain curves) is reported in connection with the KIC calculation of the hardest (aged) sample (b0023), so it cannot be unambiguously attributed to the solution-treated state and is therefore not entered as this sample's youngs_modulus.

Sample preparation for Vickers/EBSD/SEM/XRD was electrolytic polishing with 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol; TEM foils were mechanically ground to ~90 µm, punched to 3 mm discs and ion thinned (b0017).
